rendering.persona_description: Kofi is a 37-year-old administrative assistant at a community health clinic. He's been with his partner Dana for six years and they share a two-bedroom apartment on the east side of town. Outside of work he coaches a youth soccer team on weekends and has kept the same close group of friends since college.
rendering.clinical_context: Kofi has obsessive-compulsive disorder with a doubt and checking theme, focused mainly on locks, the stove, and whether he's taken his own medications correctly. Symptoms started in his mid-20s during a cross-country move and got worse gradually; he was diagnosed about ten years ago after his morning checking routine started taking over an hour. He's four months into a course of exposure and response prevention, his first structured treatment, and has recently started wondering out loud whether it's worth continuing.
rendering.behavioral_description: Kofi talks in a lot of concrete detail about specific incidents: the exact number of times he checked the deadbolt, what he pictured happening if he hadn't. He'll listen to a counterpoint and turn it over for a minute, sometimes conceding a small piece, but he circles back to defending why his worry is reasonable in this particular case. He gets clipped and a little defensive if he feels like he's being told his concerns aren't real, though he doesn't shut down entirely.
